1.explanation:
1. lib/features/replace/BpmnReplace.js
   • Contains the core replaceElement logic that copies the old element’s width/height into the new subprocess when converting to an expanded subprocess. Because it always preserves the prior task dimensions, the expanded subprocess never grows to its default size.

2. lib/features/modeling/behavior/ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.js
   • Handles resizing when a subprocess is collapsed or expanded via toggleCollapse, but that command is never invoked on initial replace. As a result, no resize is applied on conversion from call activity → expanded subprocess.

3. lib/features/replace/ReplaceOptions.js
   • Defines both “collapsed” and “expanded” subprocess options for the replace menu, even though a collapsed subprocess isn’t fully supported in the UI. This leads to confusing extra menu entries.

4. lib/features/popup-menu/ReplaceMenuProvider.js
   • Gathers and filters replace options for the wrench menu. It doesn’t filter out unsupported collapsed-subprocess actions when the element is a call activity, and once converted to expanded subprocess it only offers “event sub-process,” preventing the user from switching back to call activity.
1.bug_scenario: After transforming a task into a call activity via the wrench (“replace”) menu, two new entries — “sub-process collapsed” and “sub-process expanded” — appear. Choosing “sub-process expanded” replaces the call activity with an expanded subprocess, but the shape remains the size of the original task (instead of resizing to the subprocess default). Once in this state, the wrench menu only shows “event sub-process” as an option, so you cannot revert back to a call activity and you reach a dead end.
